summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics). This update turns the freshness probe into an execution-grounded conclusion: child question 70ce3ecb3bba4649bed736cbf499b3ae-question-0 now has an interpretation for its own experiment 70ce3ecb3bba4649bed736cbf499b3ae-experiment with conclusion violated, citing receipt eb708864312549dfb0440dded9b2e359 (completed, exit 0, tests_passed, no parsing errors, 6 parsed events) at decisive parsed indices 1, 2, 4, 5. Predicate as declared: when a second ReadIndex admission reuses an rctx that is still pending, the answer carrying that rctx has an index at least as new as the commit index observed at the second admission. It is violated at index 2 - the second admission happened with committed_at_admission 2 while pending and queue stayed at 1 (no status of its own), a write had already been committed in between, and the single answer carrying that rctx reported answer_index 1 with answer_index_at_least_admission false, i.e. the index recorded at the first admission. The distinct-rctx control holds at index 5 (pending/queue 2, answer_index 2, answers 2), which isolates rctx coalescing as the cause and is backed by the already-recorded producer behaviour that only the first admission stores a request message and index. A Fact entry records the observed instance with its receipt and operands, and the question is marked explained with the parent liveness question left intact. Counterevidence keeps the contract caveat prominent - release-3.6 documents that callers must not reuse an rctx while the same comment says the restriction is lifted from release-3.7, so the classification of the stale index as a defect is left to human review, alongside the harness-held heartbeat ordering, the single interleaving, and the application-side ReadState matching that lies outside the captured package. No new experiment is requested this turn.
